lines.text: Dune banned AI in nineteen sixty-five.
Not as a plot twist. As the foundation of the entire universe.
Long before the story starts, humanity fights a holy war against thinking machines.
It's called the Butlerian Jihad.
And that name? Real. Samuel Butler, eighteen sixty-three.
A letter to a New Zealand newspaper, warning machines might replace us as the dominant species.
Eighteen sixty-three. That's thirteen years before the telephone.
Somebody was already worried about AI.
So with machines banned, who does the maths?
People. Mentats. Human computers, trained to store data and calculate on demand.
Basically a laptop that needs lunch.
And here's the part that got me.
The word computer meant a person first. Oxford's earliest record is sixteen thirteen. One who computes.
So did Dune predict the AI wars?
Not exactly. It asked the question we're arguing about right now.
Dune's answer: ban it. Ours: ship it, fix it later.
And Dune Part Three lands December eighteenth.
A ban in fiction.
A warning from eighteen sixty-three.
And a job title that used to be human.
So be honest. If you could press the button and ban thinking machines, would you?
Pick a side in the comments.
Follow for more. Next: why games have loading screens.
